newsitem.title: UK: Shell Rotterdam returns to full production - trade.
newsitem.headline: Shell Rotterdam returns to full production - trade.

text.p: Shell has restored its Rotterdam refinery to full production to take advantage of the boost in margins generated by the fall in crude prices, trading sources said on Monday.
The refinery, which has a normal throughput of 350,000 barrel per day (bpd) of crude, had been running at some 12-15 percent below capacity since March 4.
It was restored to full production in the middle of last week, traders said. The plant's nameplate capacity is 374,000 bpd.
The March cutback was part of a wave of run cuts in the European refining industry by operators trying to stem the losses on running their plant.
A complex refining plant running Brent crude made on average only $1.24 a barrel in profit during February, a figure that climbed to $1.46 in March.
A European hydroskimming plant was running at an average nine cent loss in February, according to Reuters price data.
Brent crude fell by nearly nine percent last week and complex European refineries are now enjoying margins of around $2.30 a barrel.
Most other big European refineries are understood to be once again working at full capacity.
